newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Micronesia landslides kill eight, emergency declared.
newsitem.headline: Micronesia landslides kill eight, emergency declared.

text.p: Officials have declared a state of emergency in Pohnpei in the Federated States of Micronesia after landslides killed eight people and left another eight missing, police from the Pacific island said on Wednesday.

Four other people were injured in the landslides that crushed 10 hillside houses in Sokehs municipality during heavy rains and widespread flooding on Monday, national police sergeant John Johnnyboy said by telephone from Pohnpei.
"Those are indefinite figures. We are still searching for people," Johnnyboy said. "There were landslides all around the island."
The eight missing "are probably also dead", he said.
The rains and floods also caused heavy damage to crops, he added.
Micronesia is a string of islands in the Pacific halfway between the Philippines and Hawaii with a population of about 105,000, nearly half of them in Pohnpei, police said.
Under the emergency declared by Micronesian President Jacob Nena, all civil servants were required to report to work to help in rescue and rehabiliation efforts, police said.
A week before the floods and landslides occurred, a typhoon battered the islands, killing a fisherman at sea, they said.
